1.explanation:
• src/lib/monitor-adapter.js: This adapter is responsible for pulling the slider’s metadata (min, max, step) out of the VM’s monitor payload and shuttling it through props. It’s currently empty/missing, so no custom range ever makes it into the component.
• src/components/monitor/slider-monitor.jsx: The SliderMonitor component hard-codes defaultProps of min: 0 and max: 100. Even if we wire up the adapter, these default values will override custom ranges unless we remove or adjust them.
• src/containers/slider-monitor.jsx: This container passes props through to the component but never handles any custom min/max values from the VM; it simply reads props.value. It needs to accept and forward the range fields.
• src/containers/monitor.jsx: The main Monitor container calls monitorAdapter and then spreads its return into the MonitorComponent, passing min, max, and isDiscrete. Without proper adapter output here, the slider mode and range controls will always get the fixed defaults.
1.bug_scenario: When you import a Scratch 2.0 project that has a slider monitor with a custom minimum and maximum, the slider in Scratch 3.0 still shows the default 0–100 range. Right-clicking the slider monitor in 3.0 brings up the “Slider Range” dialog with Min: 0 and Max: 100 (see screenshot), even if the imported project specified a different range.
